questions.question: Define scalene, isosceles and equilateral triangles, and say which name a triangle with three equal sides receives in a classification.
questions.expected_answer: Scalene: no two sides equal. Isosceles: at least two sides equal. Equilateral: all three sides equal. A triangle with three equal sides is called equilateral, the more specific name, although it also satisfies the isosceles definition.

questions.question: Why can an equilateral triangle never be right-angled or obtuse-angled?
questions.expected_answer: Three equal sides give three equal angles, and the three angles add to 180 degrees, so each is 60. Every angle is acute, so the triangle is always acute-angled; a right or obtuse angle would require unequal angles and therefore unequal sides.

questions.question: Two angles of a triangle are 35 and 55 degrees. Classify the triangle by angles and explain.
questions.expected_answer: The third angle is 180 minus 35 minus 55, which is 90 degrees. The largest angle is exactly 90, so the triangle is right-angled; the two given angles are complementary and the side opposite the 90 is the hypotenuse.
